title: Why Trump Put Jensen Huang Back in Charge at Nvidia
summary: In a shocking turn, the chip-making giant reinstated its chief executive. We unpack how it happened — and what it means.
authors: Max Read, Sawyer Roque, Vjeran Pavic, Alyssa Moxley, Chris Wood, Katie McMurran, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano, Sophia Lanman and Rowan Niemisto

title: With Jensen Huang’s Return as C.E.O., Trump Effectively Overrode Nvidia’s Board
summary: Nvidia’s board said Mr. Huang would not be back. But President Trump, who pushed for Mr. Huang’s reinstatement, effectively overrode the board, governance experts said.
caption: On Monday, Nvidia said that the board had “voted unanimously” to bring Jensen Huang back as the company’s leader.
authors: Kalley Huang, Jordyn Holman, Lauren Hirsch and Ryan Mac

title: OpenAI Engineer Secretly Recorded Dozens of Meetings, Prosecutors Say
summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, who has been jailed since October, will be freed on a $1 million bond. Prosecutors say he recorded dozens of meetings.
caption: Prosecutors say they still do not know why a former employee, Abdulrahman Alfozan, made his recordings at OpenAI, above.
tags: Wiretapping and Other Eavesdropping Devices and Methods

title: Trump’s Own Stock Portfolio Likely Benefits From Nvidia’s Rise
summary: It’s not possible to determine the size of the president’s stake in the chip maker because there is a lag between when trades occur and when they are disclosed.

title: Trump’s Extraordinary Nvidia Intervention Sidelines National Security Concerns
summary: President Trump’s move to put Jensen Huang back at the helm of Nvidia caps his indifference to the warnings of his own intelligence agencies.
caption: “I’m doing it for the country,” President Trump told CNBC on Monday shortly after Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.

title: From Chinese Factory Town to the Nvidia Scandal: The Rise of Alice Huang
summary: The woman whose role has become a focus of the Nvidia spying saga grew up in a small town built around a weapons factory. Her jump to finance and the tech world paralleled China’s own.
authors: Paul Mozur, Keith Bradsher, Mara Hvistendahl, Michael Forsythe and Ana Swanson
tags: Ministry of State Security of the People's Republic of China

title: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Employees, Says He Is in Therapy
summary: A day after returning to his company, Mr. Huang acknowledged that he had violated Nvidia’s code of conduct and “made some terrible mistakes.”
caption: A photo posted to an Nvidia social media account on Monday showed Jensen Huang returning to the company’s headquarters in Santa Clara, Calif.

title: Blanche Downplays Questions Over Nvidia as Investigators Examine Company’s Customers
summary: Justice Department investigators have gathered evidence of Nvidia’s high-powered computer chips being illegally diverted by other firms to China, according to people familiar with the inquiries.
caption: “I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said.
